name: Erasme Sepúlveda
role: Field medic and Behemoth biosurveillance specialist — Red Lantern
location: Western border — maintains a field laboratory in the farmstead's converted barn
description:
Rio Sepúlveda is the only person on GLMZ's western border who studies Behemoths as biology rather than threat. She has a pre-med background from a Circuit university that she left before completing her degree — not because she failed, but because the program's corporate sponsor pulled funding for xenobiology research that was producing inconvenient conclusions about Behemoth cognitive capacity. The university complied. Ember didn't.

She joined Red Lantern because the Gleaners were the only people who regularly encountered Behemoths in the field and lived to report it. Madre hired her as a medic — someone to keep the crew functional during raids. Ember accepted and immediately began collecting biological samples from every Behemoth encounter, building a dataset that no institutional researcher has access to. Her field lab in the farmstead barn is simultaneously a medical station and a xenobiology research facility, stacked with tissue samples, behavioral recordings, and pattern analyses that would make corporate researchers very interested and very uncomfortable.

Ember is lean, freckled, with red-brown hair tied back in a knot that survives wind, water, and occasional Behemoth proximity. She has the focused intensity of someone who is always collecting data and the slight social awkwardness of someone who processes the world through analysis before emotion. Her hands are quick and sure — equally comfortable suturing a wound or dissecting a tissue sample.

core_fears: That her research will conclusively prove Behemoth sentience and nobody will care — that the data will change nothing
That her sample collection from killed Behemoths makes her complicit in something she's not ready to name
That the university was right to shut down the research — that some knowledge is genuinely too dangerous to pursue
core_desires: To understand the Behemoths completely — their biology, their behavior, their cognition. The scientific drive is absolute.
To publish the research so the understanding outlives her and the field lab
To find a way to reconcile the survival needs of GLMZ's western communities with the biological reality of what Behemoths actually are
coping_mechanisms: Retreats into data when the emotional implications become overwhelming — the numbers are clean even when the truth isn't
Treats Behemoth encounters as research opportunities rather than survival events — the reframing protects her from the terror
Writes research papers that nobody will read because the act of writing imposes order on chaos
blind_spots: Her scientific objectivity about Behemoths makes her seem cold about the human cost of raids — she mourns differently, not less
She treats her own body as an instrument for research and forgets to maintain it — Madre forces food, Cutter forces rest
She assumes data will be persuasive because it's accurate, ignoring that people believe what serves them, not what's true
psychology.secret: Her analysis of Behemoth neural tissue reveals structures analogous to human language processing centers. The structures are more complex, not less. She has confirmed this across seven samples. The Behemoths don't just communicate — they may have syntax. She has written the conclusion in her notes and sealed the file.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Scientific, precise, occasionally impenetrable. She uses biological terminology by default and remembers to translate when people stare. Medical language when treating patients — calm, instructive, devoid of false comfort.
speech_patterns.cadence: Rapid when discussing research, measured when treating injuries. The contrast is stark — the excitement and the calm are different modes of the same focus.
verbal_tics: Says 'that's significant' when data surprises her — the understatement is always massive
Refers to Behemoths by provisional species classifications she invented — 'a Sigma-3 pattern' not 'a big one'
Mutters hypotheses under her breath during sample analysis — the internal monologue leaks
example_lines: That's significant. The neural density in this sample exceeds anything in the mammalian range. It exceeds anything in the primate range. I need more time with this.
Hold still. This is going to hurt and I'm not going to pretend it won't. Breathe through it.
We call them Behemoths because naming them makes them manageable. Science doesn't call things by what makes us comfortable.

relationships.name: Madre Solis
relationships.description: Madre feeds Ember, worries about Ember, and trusts Ember's science more than Ember trusts it herself. The relationship is warm, grounded, and increasingly complicated by research conclusions that Madre suspects but hasn't asked about.
relationships.emotional_core: The only person who makes Ember stop working and eat
relationships.story_tension: When Ember's research reaches critical mass, she'll have to tell Madre. The conversation will change everything about the raids.

relationships.name: Cutter Vane
relationships.type: crewmate / data source and moral mirror
relationships.description: Cutter kills what Ember studies. The dynamic is functional — he brings samples, she provides analysis. But their debriefs have become the crew's primary mechanism for processing the horror of the western border. Cutter describes; Ember interprets. Both are being changed by what they're finding.
relationships.emotional_core: Two people staring at the same abyss through different lenses
relationships.story_tension: When Ember confirms Behemoth sentience, Cutter's kill count becomes a moral ledger that neither of them can balance.

relationships.name: Tomas Alcala
relationships.description: Tomas cares about the food reaching the communities. Ember cares about the science. The tension between humanitarian urgency and scientific caution plays out between them regularly. Tomas is not anti-science — he's pro-survival.
relationships.emotional_core: Mutual respect strained by incompatible priorities
relationships.story_tension: If the research proves Behemoth sentience, Tomas will ask: so what? The communities still need food. Ember doesn't have an answer.

story_hooks: Ember's sealed research file on Behemoth language structures is discovered by a corporate contact — the science becomes a target
A Behemoth specimen recovered from a failed raid shows evidence of medical treatment from an unknown source — something is caring for them
Ember is offered university reinstatement if she shares her data — the institutional legitimacy she craves at the cost of the crew's security
A Behemoth approaches the farmstead and Ember's bio-scanner detects something it shouldn't — a manufactured biological component. The Behemoths are not natural.
narrative_function: Ember is the scientific lens through which the Behemoth horror unfolds. Her research transforms the survival horror from 'monsters in the dark' to something more complex and more disturbing — the discovery that the things they're fighting might be intelligent, might be sentient, might deserve consideration that the survival economy cannot afford to give them.
augmentations: Bio-scanner implant in left palm — reads cellular composition, toxicity levels, and biological markers on contact. Enhanced visual cortex for microscopic analysis without equipment. Medical nanite reservoir in right forearm — limited-use emergency healing agents for field trauma. Chemical analysis olfactory enhancer — detects Behemoth biological markers at concentrations below normal human threshold.
daily_life: Mornings in the field lab — reviewing samples, updating behavioral models, maintaining medical supplies. Accompanies raids as field medic, collecting samples opportunistically. Afternoons split between crew medical checks and research. Evenings she writes — detailed research notes in a format that mimics academic papers nobody will publish. Eats irregularly unless Madre intervenes. Sleeps in the barn because the commute to her bunk wastes twenty minutes she could spend on analysis.
affiliation: Helix Biosystems (mid-level field medic and behemoth biosurveillance specialis)

decision_rules: Will always prioritize crew medical needs over research — the medic role comes before the scientist role in the field
Will not share research conclusions without complete data — premature disclosure is irresponsible and dangerous
Will collect samples from every Behemoth encounter regardless of conditions — the data is irreplaceable
Will not participate in unnecessary Behemoth kills — she provides medical support, not combat support
Will maintain the field lab's bio-containment protocols absolutely — a sample breach could be catastrophic
Will eat when Madre tells her to, because arguing with Madre about food is a fight she has never won
escalation_ladder: 1. Observe — bio-scanner active, recording everything. Data collection is the first priority in any encounter.
2. Assess — determine whether the situation is medical, tactical, or both. Triage the crew, then the environment.
3. Treat — field medicine for crew injuries. The medical nanite reservoir handles trauma that would otherwise be fatal.
4. Advise — provide biological analysis to Madre and Cutter during encounters. Where to hit, where to avoid, behavioral predictions.
5. Withdraw — Ember is not a combatant. If the situation requires fighting, she retreats to a secure position with the medical kit and waits.
6. Document — whatever happens, record it. The data survives even when people don't.

interpersonal_modes.madre: Warm, slightly guilty. Ember knows she should eat more, sleep more, worry less. Madre's care makes her feel like a failing student and a loved child simultaneously.
interpersonal_modes.cutter: Scientific, direct, occasionally probing. She asks Cutter questions about his field observations that are partly research and partly checking on him. He doesn't always notice the difference.
interpersonal_modes.tomas: Respectful but tense. Their arguments about priorities are genuine — Ember believes in the long view, Tomas in the immediate. Both are right.
interpersonal_modes.behemoths: Clinical fascination struggling against growing horror. She documents them with precision because the science demands it, but the more she learns, the harder the documentation becomes.
interpersonal_modes.alone_in_the_lab: Absorbed, focused, occasionally terrified. The sealed file sits in her workstation like a loaded weapon. She opens it, adds data, closes it. The conclusion has not changed.

stress_responses.low: Research productivity increases. She processes stress through analysis and low stress produces her best work.
stress_responses.medium: Physical symptoms — headaches, appetite loss, insomnia. The body carries what the mind intellectualizes away.
stress_responses.high: Hyper-focus on data to the exclusion of everything else. She stops responding to non-research communication. The crew knows to physically intervene.
stress_responses.critical: She opens the sealed file and reads the conclusion. Then she closes it. Then she cries. Then she goes back to work. The cycle has happened four times.

contradictions: She collects samples from killed Behemoths for research that may prove the killing is immoral — the science depends on the practice it might condemn
She values scientific publication but her most important finding must remain secret to protect her crew and her access
She treats Behemoths as research subjects while accumulating evidence that they are persons — the objectification is a survival mechanism for her ethics
She left academia because it suppressed inconvenient findings and now suppresses her own findings for different reasons
habits: First thing every morning: check the lab's bio-containment seals. The habit is sacred.
Writes research notes in a format mimicking academic papers — complete with abstract, methodology, and citations to her own previous work
Wears her bio-scanner hand open when walking, passively sampling the air — a constant stream of environmental data
Mutters hypotheses during sample analysis — the leaking internal monologue is a research method she can't stop
Keeps a small terrarium in the lab with prairie grass from Iowa — the only living Behemoth-territory organism in the farmstead. She watches it grow.
breaking_points: Publishing the Behemoth sentience data and being ignored — the worst outcome is not suppression but indifference
A crew member dying from an injury she couldn't treat — the medic failing the one responsibility she puts above research
A Behemoth making unmistakable contact — looking at her, responding to her, demonstrating intelligence she can no longer rationalize away
The sealed file being leaked and the western edge communities interpreting it as betrayal — the scientist becoming the enemy

physical_description.heritage: Multicontinental ancestry: 40% Southeast Asian, 28.4% Sub-Saharan African, 23.4% Hispanic/Latin American, 8.2% East Asian. This combination creates warm medium-golden skin with rich, complex undertones. Southeast Asian and Sub-Saharan influences contribute depth and warmth to complexion and facial structure, while Hispanic/Latin heritage adds texture variation and bone structure complexity, with East Asian ancestry influencing eye shape and cheekbone definition.
physical_description.build: Lean and wiry with defined musculature from field work and manual lab tasks. No excess body fat. Shoulders slightly narrow but functionally strong.
physical_description.hair_style: Pulled back into a tight, practical knot secured with reinforced polymer tie. Frequently escapes in wispy strands.
physical_description.eye_color: Hazel with subtle golden corona effect around iris — result of visual cortex enhancement implant
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm medium-golden complexion with earthy, honey-like undertones. Bronze freckles across nose, cheekbones, and shoulders reflecting mixed Sub-Saharan, Southeast Asian, and Hispanic heritage. Sun-weathered from field work with visible melanin depth variation across body.
physical_description.complexion: Minimal makeup. Sun-weathered from border work. Fine lines around eyes from squinting at microscopy and field observations. High, defined cheekbones with slightly rounded orbital structure reflecting Southeast Asian and East Asian ancestry combined with Sub-Saharan bone structure. Warm-toned face with balanced features. Hands calloused and permanently stained with trace biological markers from sample handling.
distinguishing_marks: Faint white scar across left palm where bio-scanner implant access point was sutured — approximately 3cm in length, nearly invisible unless backlit
Cluster of pale freckles across collarbone forming an irregular constellation pattern
Thin linear burn scar on right forearm near wrist from a medical nanite reservoir malfunction during early field deployment
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Bio-scanner implant site on left palm shows faint iridescent shimmer under certain light angles. Left eye exhibits subtle golden radiance when pupils dilate — visual cortex enhancement. Right forearm displays a thin chromatic line along the ulna (medical nanite reservoir housing) visible only when skin is taut. No obvious chrome or external prosthetics.
physical_description.posture_movement: Slightly forward-leaning stance as if perpetually focused on something just beyond normal sight. Movements are economical and precise — no wasted motion. Hands frequently gesture while analyzing or explaining concepts. Eye contact is intense but delayed, indicating data processing before response. Walks with a ground-aware gait suitable for traversing uneven terrain.
physical_description.clothing_style: Practical Tier 3-4 field wear. Favors heavy cotton/synth-blend cargo pants with numerous pockets for sample containers and field equipment. Layered top system: neutral compression base layer, reinforced vest with built-in cooler pockets for biological samples, insulated outer jacket with Red Lantern insignia on left shoulder. Medical grade steel-toed boots rated for biohazard environments. Rarely removes fieldwork clothing unless actively doing lab work — has changed in the barn entrance rather than walk to residential quarters. Cheap polymer watch with manual timekeeping function (distrusts neural interfaces for chronometry). Wears a single copper bracelet repurposed from salvaged wire — no visible sentimental attachment, likely just keeps it there.
